description: Queue Instance: Instance of a cluster queue on an execution host

attributes.name: qhostname
description: The host this queue instance runs on. Together with QU_qname it identifies the instance.

attributes.name: qname
description: @todo add description

attributes.name: full_name
description: The instance name as users see it, "cluster_queue@host". Derived from QU_qname and QU_qhostname; do not set it directly.

attributes.name: tag
description: Scratch marker used while a cluster queue change is applied, holding SGE_QI_TAG_ADD, _MOD or _DEL for this instance. Not persistent.

attributes.name: available_at
description: Earliest time this instance could run the job being scheduled, set during resource matching and used to order the candidates.

attributes.name: seq_no
description: Position of this queue in the scheduling order, used when the scheduler is configured to sort queues by sequence number rather than by load.

attributes.name: nsuspend
description: How many jobs are suspended at once when a suspend threshold is exceeded, and resumed at once when it falls back.

attributes.name: qtype
description: Whether the queue accepts batch jobs, interactive jobs, or both.

attributes.name: job_slots
description: How many jobs may run in this instance at once. The scheduler compares it against the slots already used.

attributes.name: tmpdir
description: Where the execution daemon creates the per-job temporary directory it advertises as $TMPDIR.

attributes.name: shell
description: The shell a job script is started with, when the start mode calls for one.

attributes.name: calendar
description: The calendar that enables, disables or suspends this queue by time of day and day of week.

attributes.name: priority
description: The nice value jobs in this queue are started with.

attributes.name: processors
description: The processor set jobs are bound to, on the platforms that support one.

attributes.name: prolog
description: A command run as a preamble before the job, in the job's environment. A non-zero exit puts the queue into error state.

attributes.name: epilog
description: A command run after the job, in the job's environment, whatever the job's own exit status was.

attributes.name: shell_start_mode
description: How the job script is handed to the shell: as a script argument, on stdin, or by exec.

attributes.name: starter_method
description: Replaces the default way of starting the job, for jobs that need a wrapper.

attributes.name: suspend_method
description: Replaces the default SIGSTOP when the job is suspended.

attributes.name: resume_method
description: Replaces the default SIGCONT when the job is resumed.

attributes.name: terminate_method
description: Replaces the default SIGKILL when the job is deleted.

attributes.name: initial_state
description: The state the instance takes when it is first created or when its execution daemon restarts: enabled, disabled, or whatever it was.

attributes.name: rerun
description: Default for jobs whose execution host crashed: rerun them elsewhere, or report them as failed. A job may override it with qsub -r.

attributes.name: s_rt
description: Wall clock time after which the job is warned with SIGUSR1 and then killed once QU_notify has passed.

attributes.name: h_rt
description: Wall clock time after which the job is killed outright.

attributes.name: s_cpu
description: Combined CPU time of all the job's processes after which it is sent SIGXCPU.

attributes.name: h_cpu
description: Combined CPU time after which the job is killed.

attributes.name: s_fsize
description: Largest file the job may create before it is warned.

attributes.name: h_fsize
description: Largest file the job may create.

attributes.name: s_data
description: Data segment size after which the job is warned.

attributes.name: h_data
description: Largest data segment the job may allocate.

attributes.name: s_stack
description: Stack size after which the job is warned.

attributes.name: h_stack
description: Largest stack the job may use.

attributes.name: s_core
description: Core file size after which the job is warned.

attributes.name: h_core
description: Largest core file the job may write.

attributes.name: s_rss
description: Resident set size after which the job is warned.

attributes.name: h_rss
description: Largest resident set the job may hold.

attributes.name: s_vmem
description: Virtual memory after which the job is warned. For a parallel job the limit applies per slot on the host.

attributes.name: h_vmem
description: Virtual memory after which the job is killed. For a parallel job the limit applies per slot on the host.

attributes.name: suspend_interval
description: How long to wait between two suspend rounds, so a threshold is not acted on faster than the load can react.

attributes.name: min_cpu_interval
description: Shortest time between two automatic checkpoints, whatever shorter interval the checkpointing environment or the job asks for.

attributes.name: notify
description: How long to wait between the warning signal and the real suspend or kill signal, for jobs submitted with qsub -notify.

attributes.name: ckpt_list
description: The checkpointing environments a job may request here.

attributes.name: pe_list
description: The parallel environments a job may request here.

attributes.name: owner_list
description: Users allowed to suspend, resume and disable this queue without being managers or operators.

attributes.name: acl
description: The usersets allowed to run jobs here. Empty means everyone who is not in QU_xacl.

attributes.name: xacl
description: The usersets not allowed to run jobs here. Checked before QU_acl.

attributes.name: projects
description: The projects whose jobs may run here.

attributes.name: xprojects
description: The projects whose jobs may not run here.

attributes.name: consumable_config_list
description: The consumable capacities of this instance, as configured. QU_resource_utilization tracks what is actually booked against them.

attributes.name: load_thresholds
description: Load values above which the queue stops accepting jobs. Reaching one puts the instance into alarm state (the "a" in qstat).

attributes.name: suspend_thresholds
description: Load values above which jobs already running here are suspended, QU_nsuspend at a time.

attributes.name: subordinate_list
description: Queues to suspend while this one is busy, either wholesale or per slot. What implements the "S" state on the other queue.

attributes.name: state
description: The QI_* state bits, and the letters qstat prints for them. Eleven independent flags; see sge_qinstance_state.cc.

attributes.name: tagged4schedule
description: used for parallel job scheduling only
0 - can be used only as slave queue
1 - can be used as slave queue for now assignment,
however as master for reservation
2 - can be used as master for now and reservation

attributes.name: cache_version
description: @warning Read and written nowhere in either repository. Kept because removing an attribute changes the spooled format.

attributes.name: pending_signal
description: A signal sent to the queue that has not taken effect yet. Kept until the state changes, so it can be repeated.

attributes.name: pending_signal_delivery_time
description: When to send QU_pending_signal again. Spooled, so a qmaster restart does not lose an in-flight signal.

attributes.name: version
description: Incremented by qinstance_increase_qversion() on every change. A scheduler order carries the version it was computed against, and sge_follow() rejects the order if the queue has moved on.

attributes.name: suspended_on_subordinate
description: How many superordinate queues currently demand that this one be suspended. A count, not a flag, so releasing one does not resume a queue another still holds down.

attributes.name: last_suspend_threshold_ckeck
description: When the suspend thresholds were last evaluated, so they are not acted on more often than QU_suspend_interval.

attributes.name: job_cnt
description: @warning Read and written nowhere in either repository. Kept because removing an attribute changes the spooled format.

attributes.name: pending_job_cnt
description: @warning Read and written nowhere in either repository. Kept because removing an attribute changes the spooled format.

attributes.name: soft_violation
description: How many of the job's soft requests this instance cannot satisfy. The scheduler sorts candidates by this ascending, so a queue that grants more soft requests wins.

attributes.name: host_seq_no
description: The host's position in the scheduler's host sort order, copied onto the instance while tagging so queues on a better host sort first.

attributes.name: resource_utilization
description: What is actually booked against each consumable over time, including future bookings made by advance reservations. The counterpart of QU_consumable_config_list.

attributes.name: message_list
description: Messages explaining the instance's state, shown by qstat -explain and qrstat.

attributes.name: gdi_do_later
description: Marks the instance as having a change that is applied after the current request rather than during it.

attributes.name: state_changes
description: new state variables, these are needed for the scheduler, to dispach jobs into suitable queues

attributes.name: joker
description: Placeholder which can be used for arbitrary data.
Its purpose is to be able to add new attributes without changing the spooling format.
It is a list of arbitrary type and it is spooled.
